title: Ezekiel Chapter 25 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 25 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 25 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 25.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 25, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came again unto me
Set thy face against the Ammonites
I will make Rabbah a stable for camels
Because thou hast clapped thine hands and stamped with the feet
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came again unto me
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:1 states 'The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying,' which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: Who did the Lord command Ezekiel to prophesy against in Ezekiel 25?
options: The Ammonites
The Babylonians
The Egyptians
The Moabites
questions.correctAnswer: The Ammonites
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:2 states 'Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them;'

questions.question: What did the Ammonites say against the sanctuary according to Ezekiel 25?
options: Aha
Woe
Alas
Behold
questions.correctAnswer: Aha
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:3 says 'Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned;'

questions.question: To whom will the LORD deliver the Ammonites according to Ezekiel 25?
options: Men of the east
Babylonians
Egyptians
Assyrians
questions.correctAnswer: Men of the east
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 states 'Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession,'

questions.question: What will the men of the east do in Ammon's land?
options: Set their palaces and make their dwellings
Destroy the cities
Build walls around the land
Plant vineyards
questions.correctAnswer: Set their palaces and make their dwellings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 says 'they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee;'

questions.question: What will the men of the east eat and drink from Ammon?
options: Fruit and milk
Grain and water
Meat and wine
Fish and oil
questions.correctAnswer: Fruit and milk
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 states 'they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk.'

questions.question: What will Rabbah be made into as per Ezekiel 25?
options: A stable for camels
A city of gold
A fortress
A place of worship
questions.correctAnswer: A stable for camels
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:5 says 'And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels,'

questions.question: What will the Ammonites become according to Ezekiel 25:5?
options: A couching place for flocks
A land of milk and honey
A city of refuge
A vineyard
questions.correctAnswer: A couching place for flocks
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:5 states 'and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks:'

questions.question: What will the Ammonites know after these things happen?
options: That I am the LORD
That they will be victorious
That their land will prosper
That they will be forgiven
questions.correctAnswer: That I am the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:5 concludes with 'and ye shall know that I am the LORD.'

questions.question: What actions did the Ammonites do against Israel as mentioned in Ezekiel 25?
options: Clapped hands, stamped feet, and rejoiced in heart
Built altars, offered sacrifices, and prayed
Wept and fasted
Sent gifts and messengers
questions.correctAnswer: Clapped hands, stamped feet, and rejoiced in heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:6 states 'Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel;'

questions.question: Against whom did the Ammonites rejoice according to Ezekiel 25?
options: The land of Israel
The house of Judah
The men of the east
The sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:6 says '...rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel;'

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came again unto Ezekiel in Ezekiel 25.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:1 states 'The word of the LORD came again unto me,' confirming this fact.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was commanded to prophesy against the Ammonites in Ezekiel 25.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:2 commands 'Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them;'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 25 says the Ammonites will be given gold and silver as a possession.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 states the Ammonites will be delivered to the men of the east as a possession, but it does not mention gold or silver.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 25 mentions the Ammonites building new walls around their cities.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention the Ammonites building walls anywhere in Ezekiel 25.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 25 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 25 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:7, what will happen to Moab as a consequence of their actions?
options: I will stretch out mine hand upon thee and deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen
I will bless thee and multiply thy people
I will establish peace and prosperity in thy land
I will send prophets to guide thy people
questions.correctAnswer: I will stretch out mine hand upon thee and deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:7 states that God will stretch out His hand upon Moab and deliver them for a spoil to the heathen as judgment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 25:7 promise will happen if Moab and Seir say, 'Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen' as mentioned in Ezekiel 25:8?
options: God will open the side of Moab from the cities on his frontiers
God will bless Moab and Seir for their honesty
God will ignore their words and show favor to Judah
God will send a prophet to warn them
questions.correctAnswer: God will open the side of Moab from the cities on his frontiers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:8 and 25:9 connect that because Moab and Seir said Judah is like all heathen, God will open the side of Moab from the cities on his frontiers.

questions.question: Which cities are specifically mentioned as being opened up in Moab according to Ezekiel 25:9?
options: Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim
Rabbah, Ammon, and Seir
Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and Hebron
Nineveh, Babylon, and Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:9 names the cities Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim as those opened up in Moab.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:10-11, what is the purpose of giving Moab's cities to the men of the east with the Ammonites?
options: So the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations
So Moab will prosper under new leadership
To establish peace between Moab and Ammon
To create a new alliance with Judah
questions.correctAnswer: So the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:10 explains that the Ammonites will possess Moab's cities so that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations, and verse 11 confirms judgments upon Moab.

questions.question: How does God describe His judgment upon the Ammonites in Ezekiel 25:4?
options: Delivering them to the men of the east for a possession
Blessing them with abundance
Protecting their land from enemies
Granting them peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Delivering them to the men of the east for a possession
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 states that God will deliver the Ammonites to the men of the east for a possession as a judgment.

questions.question: What symbolic imagery is used in Ezekiel 25:5 to describe what will happen to Rabbah and the Ammonites?
options: Rabbah as a stable for camels and Ammonites a couching place for flocks
Rabbah as a fortified city and Ammonites as mighty warriors
Rabbah as a garden and Ammonites as fruitful trees
Rabbah as a prison and Ammonites as captives
questions.correctAnswer: Rabbah as a stable for camels and Ammonites a couching place for flocks
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:5 uses the imagery of Rabbah becoming a stable for camels and Ammonites a couching place for flocks to symbolize desolation and defeat.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:6, what behavior of the Ammonites provoked God's judgment?
options: Clapping hands, stamping feet, and rejoicing in heart with all despite against Israel
Helping the captives of Israel
Praying for the land of Israel
Offering sacrifices to God
questions.correctAnswer: Clapping hands, stamping feet, and rejoicing in heart with all despite against Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:6 explains that the Ammonites clapped their hands, stamped their feet, and rejoiced with spite against Israel, provoking God's judgment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 25:8 say about the attitude of Moab and Seir toward the house of Judah?
options: They say the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen
They honor the house of Judah as chosen by God
They seek to make peace with the house of Judah
They protect the house of Judah from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They say the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:8 states that Moab and Seir say the house of Judah is like all the heathen, indicating contempt and rejection.

questions.question: What is the intended outcome for Moab after God executes judgments upon them, according to Ezekiel 25:11?
options: They shall know that I am the LORD
They shall rise in power and glory
They shall form an alliance with Israel
They shall be blessed with peace
questions.correctAnswer: They shall know that I am the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:11 emphasizes that the purpose of judgment is so that Moab will know that the LORD is God.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:12, why is God angry with Edom?
options: Because Edom has taken vengeance and greatly offended the house of Judah
Because Edom has protected Judah's enemies
Because Edom refused to trade with Judah
Because Edom worshiped idols
questions.correctAnswer: Because Edom has taken vengeance and greatly offended the house of Judah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:12 states God’s anger toward Edom because it took vengeance and greatly offended the house of Judah.

questions.question: In practical Christian living, what does the judgment against Moab and Ammon teach about the consequences of rejoicing over others' misfortune, as seen in Ezekiel 25:6?
options: Rejoicing over others’ suffering can provoke God's judgment
It is acceptable to celebrate when enemies fall
God ignores the attitude of the heart
Rejoicing is always encouraged in every circumstance
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoicing over others’ suffering can provoke God's judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:6 shows that the Ammonites rejoiced spitefully over Israel’s captivity, which led to God’s judgment, teaching that such attitudes have consequences.

questions.question: How can knowing 'I am the LORD' as stated in Ezekiel 25:11 and 25:7 affect a believer's faith and trust in God during hardships?
options: It strengthens faith by recognizing God's sovereignty over judgment and mercy
It causes believers to fear God without hope
It encourages believers to ignore God's justice
It suggests God is indifferent to human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: It strengthens faith by recognizing God's sovereignty over judgment and mercy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:7 and 25:11 show God's actions lead to recognition of Him as LORD, which should strengthen believers’ faith in His sovereign justice.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can Christians learn from the fate of Moab and Ammon in Ezekiel 25?
options: Disrespect and hostility towards God's people results in consequences
Integrity is not important in relationships with neighbors
God rewards those who oppose His people
Judgment is random and unrelated to behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Disrespect and hostility towards God's people results in consequences
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25 describes judgment upon Moab and Ammon for their hostile actions against Judah, teaching that such behavior has consequences.

questions.question: How might prayer and seeking God’s guidance help believers avoid the path of Moab and Ammon as described in Ezekiel 25?
options: Prayer fosters humility and love, preventing pride and hostility
Prayer guarantees no problems will occur
Prayer is only for personal gain
Prayer replaces the need for obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer fosters humility and love, preventing pride and hostility
questions.explanation: The judgment against Moab and Ammon arose from pride and hostility; prayer encourages humility and love, helping believers avoid such attitudes.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 25 teach about forgiveness and the consequences of vengeance, especially regarding Edom's actions in verse 12?
options: Vengeance against God’s people results in offense and judgment
Vengeance is commendable and encouraged
Forgiveness is unnecessary in divine matters
Edom’s vengeance brought them favor
questions.correctAnswer: Vengeance against God’s people results in offense and judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:12 condemns Edom for taking vengeance and greatly offending Judah, showing that vengeance leads to judgment rather than favor.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 25 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 25.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:13, what will happen to Edom?
options: I will cut off man and beast from it and make it desolate from Teman
I will bless them with prosperity and peace
I will give them dominion over Israel
I will cause them to multiply and flourish
questions.correctAnswer: I will cut off man and beast from it and make it desolate from Teman
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:13 states that God will stretch out His hand upon Edom, cutting off man and beast and making it desolate from Teman.

questions.question: How will the Lord execute His vengeance upon Edom according to Ezekiel 25:14?
options: By the hand of His people Israel
By sending a plague upon them
By raising a foreign army against them
By causing famine in their land
questions.correctAnswer: By the hand of His people Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:14 clearly states that vengeance on Edom will be laid by the hand of Israel, His people.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Ezekiel 25:15 for God's judgment on the Philistines?
options: Because they have dealt by revenge and taken vengeance with a despiteful heart
Because they worship idols
Because they refused to help Israel
Because they broke the covenant of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have dealt by revenge and taken vengeance with a despiteful heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:15 specifies that the Philistines acted with revenge and a despiteful heart, which provoked God's judgment.

questions.question: Who are the Cherethims mentioned in Ezekiel 25:16?
options: A group among the Philistines inhabiting the sea coast
A tribe of Israel
A nation allied with Moab
A group of priests in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: A group among the Philistines inhabiting the sea coast
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:16 mentions the Cherethims as part of the Philistine peoples inhabiting the sea coast, who will be cut off.

questions.question: What will happen to the remnant of the sea coast according to Ezekiel 25:16?
options: They will be destroyed along with the Cherethims
They will be spared and prosper
They will be taken captive to Babylon
They will form an alliance with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed along with the Cherethims
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:16 states that the remnant of the sea coast will be destroyed along with the Cherethims.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 25:17, what is the purpose of the great vengeance and furious rebukes executed upon the Philistines?
options: So they shall know that God is the LORD
To make them rulers over other nations
To bless them with prosperity
To restore their cities
questions.correctAnswer: So they shall know that God is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:17 declares that the vengeance is executed so that the Philistines shall know that the LORD is God.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Cherethims' (כְּרֵתִים) in Ezekiel 25:16 mean?
options: A sea-faring people or Philistine clan
A type of weapon
A fortified city
A priestly class
questions.correctAnswer: A sea-faring people or Philistine clan
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Cherethims' refers to a Philistine clan of sea-farers, often identified with the Creteans, as noted in Ezekiel 25:16.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 25:13–17 where God's vengeance is described against Edom and the Philistines?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Metaphor
Allegory
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:13–17 uses parallelism, repeating similar phrases about God's vengeance against different nations in a structured pattern.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage connects with the theme of God's vengeance upon Edom as found in Ezekiel 25:13-14?
options: Obadiah 1:10-14
Genesis 12:3
Psalm 23
Isaiah 53:5
questions.correctAnswer: Obadiah 1:10-14
questions.explanation: Obadiah 1:10-14 also prophesies judgment upon Edom for their violence against Israel, connecting with Ezekiel 25:13-14.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine vengeance and judgment found in Ezekiel 25:17?
options: Romans 12:19
John 3:16
Matthew 5:44
Philippians 4:13
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:19
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 speaks about leaving vengeance to God, echoing the theme of divine vengeance in Ezekiel 25:17.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the pronouncement against Edom in Ezekiel 25:13?
options: A judgment pronounced against Moab and Seir
A blessing upon Israel
A prophecy about Jerusalem's restoration
A lament over Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: A judgment pronounced against Moab and Seir
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:12 leads into the judgment against Edom by first addressing Moab and Seir in verses 8-11.

questions.question: In the context of Ezekiel 25:15-17, what is the significance of the 'despiteful heart' mentioned in verse 15 in Hebrew thought?
options: It implies a deep-seated, malicious intent toward others
It means ignorance of God's laws
It refers to physical illness
It denotes a joyful and forgiving spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It implies a deep-seated, malicious intent toward others
questions.explanation: The phrase 'despiteful heart' in Ezekiel 25:15 denotes malicious intent and bitter resolve, a serious offense in Hebrew ethics.

questions.question: How does the use of geographical names like Teman and Dedan in Ezekiel 25:13 contribute to the chapter's historical context?
options: They identify specific Edomite regions emphasizing the real-world impact of judgment
They symbolize heavenly places
They refer to distant Babylonian cities
They are poetic names for Israel's tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They identify specific Edomite regions emphasizing the real-world impact of judgment
questions.explanation: Teman and Dedan are known Edomite locales, grounding the prophecy historically and geographically (Ezekiel 25:13).

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 25:17 states that God's vengeance will be executed with great mercy and forgiveness toward the Philistines.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:17 states vengeance will be executed with furious rebukes, not mercy, so the correct answer is False.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 25:14 indicates that Israel will be the instrument of God's anger against Edom.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:14 says God will lay vengeance upon Edom by the hand of Israel, confirming Israel as the instrument of His anger.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 25 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 25 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 25:4 teach about God's nature regarding the judgment of nations?
options: God sovereignly uses foreign nations as instruments of judgment
God's judgment is limited to Israel and Judah only
God judges nations only based on their economic systems
God's judgment is arbitrary and without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses foreign nations as instruments of judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:4 shows that God will deliver the Ammonites to the men of the east for a possession, indicating His sovereign control over nations as instruments of judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Ezekiel 25:6 illustrate?
options: The joy in another's suffering is sin that provokes divine judgment
Sin is only personal and does not affect communal relationships
Sin is excused when it is done in ignorance
Human sin is irrelevant to God's actions
questions.correctAnswer: The joy in another's suffering is sin that provokes divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes the Ammonites clapping hands and rejoicing in the suffering of Israel, which God condemns and judges, emphasizing the sin of malicious rejoicing.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's justice is taught in Ezekiel 25:11?
options: God executes righteous judgment to reveal Himself as the LORD
God's justice is delayed indefinitely and uncertain
God judges only to punish without revealing Himself
God's justice is based on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God executes righteous judgment to reveal Himself as the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 25:11 states that God will execute judgments upon Moab so they shall know that He is the LORD, linking divine justice with self-revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 25:7 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Mercy
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 7 shows God stretching out His hand to deliver the Ammonites for a spoil, demonstrating His sovereign power over nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 25:14 especially highlight?
options: Vengeance
Grace
Patience
Omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: Vengeance
questions.explanation: In verse 14, God declares He will lay His vengeance upon Edom through Israel, highlighting His attribute of divine vengeance.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 25:12–13 connect to broader biblical themes of divine retribution against enemies of God's people?
options: It prefigures the eschatological judgment against nations opposing God's covenant
It suggests that God ignores the suffering of His people
It teaches that God favors all nations equally regardless of their actions
It indicates that God’s judgment is based solely on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the eschatological judgment against nations opposing God's covenant
questions.explanation: Verses 12–13 show God's judgment against Edom for their vengeance on Judah, reflecting the biblical motif of eschatological justice against covenant enemies.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is anticipated by Ezekiel 25:17 concerning God's vengeance?
options: The ultimate vindication of God's people and the establishment of divine justice
The defeat of Israel by surrounding nations
The abolishment of God's covenant promises
The irrelevance of divine justice in history
questions.correctAnswer: The ultimate vindication of God's people and the establishment of divine justice
questions.explanation: Verse 17 speaks of great vengeance and furious rebukes by God, which anticipates the final vindication of His people in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 25:3 and 25:6 teach about human sin and its consequences?
options: Mocking God's people leads to divine judgment revealing His holiness
Sinful actions have no impact on divine judgment
God overlooks malicious joy toward His people
Only physical destruction matters, not spiritual offenses
questions.correctAnswer: Mocking God's people leads to divine judgment revealing His holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 condemns the Ammonites for mocking Israel's desolation, and verse 6 condemns their rejoicing, together teaching that such sin brings judgment that reveals God's holiness.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's justice and sovereignty do Ezekiel 25:9 and 25:10 convey?
options: God transfers territorial possession to execute justice and fulfill His sovereign will
God's justice is limited to verbal warnings without action
God is powerless over the borders of nations
God's sovereignty is separate from His justice
questions.correctAnswer: God transfers territorial possession to execute justice and fulfill His sovereign will
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 describe God opening the cities of Moab to the men of the east and giving them to Ammonites, showing His sovereign justice through territorial transfer.

questions.question: What doctrine emerges from synthesizing Ezekiel 25:15 and 25:16 about the Philistines and divine judgment?
options: God judges out of righteous anger those who act with spite against His people
God accepts spiteful actions if they are against enemies
God's judgment is unrelated to human motives
God's vengeance is random and unjust
questions.correctAnswer: God judges out of righteous anger those who act with spite against His people
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 emphasize God's judgment on the Philistines for their revenge and hatred, teaching that God righteously judges spiteful actions against His people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 25:4-7 shows God punishing innocent nations arbitrarily. What does Ezekiel 25:3-7 actually teach?
options: God judges nations according to their hostile actions against His people and sanctuary
God punishes without cause or justice
God’s punishment is purely political and unrelated to morality
God’s judgments are random and personal
questions.correctAnswer: God judges nations according to their hostile actions against His people and sanctuary
questions.explanation: Verses 3-7 explain God's judgment on Ammon because they rejoiced over the desolation of Israel and the profaning of His sanctuary, showing just and purposeful judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 25:2 teach about prophetic responsibility?
options: Prophets are commanded to confront nations with God's judgment regardless of popular sentiment
Prophets should only speak comforting words
Prophetic messages are optional and based on personal preference
Prophets avoid pronouncing judgment to maintain peace
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets are commanded to confront nations with God's judgment regardless of popular sentiment
questions.explanation: Verse 2 commands the 'Son of man' to set his face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them, showing prophetic duty to declare God's judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially communicated in Ezekiel 25:5 regarding God's judgment?
options: Holiness
Omnipotence
Faithfulness
Patience
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 5 declares that through judgment God will make Rabbah a stable, so the nations will know He is the LORD, indicating His holy justice against defilement.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 25:13–14 contribute to the narrative arc of Israel’s restoration and divine vengeance?
options: They show that Israel will be the instrument of God's vengeance on Edom, linking restoration with retributive justice
They suggest Israel is powerless and disconnected from God's judgment
They deny any future restoration for Israel
They focus solely on Edom’s salvation
questions.correctAnswer: They show that Israel will be the instrument of God's vengeance on Edom, linking restoration with retributive justice
questions.explanation: Verses 13–14 describe God using Israel to execute vengeance on Edom, illustrating the theme of Israel’s restoration intertwined with divine justice.

questions.question: What theological synthesis arises from Ezekiel 25:1 and 25:17 about God’s revelation through judgment?
options: God reveals Himself as LORD both at the beginning and the culmination of judgment
God hides His presence during judgment
Judgment conceals God’s nature
God’s revelation is unrelated to His acts of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals Himself as LORD both at the beginning and the culmination of judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 1 introduces the word of the LORD, and verse 17 concludes that vengeance will cause the nations to know He is the LORD, framing judgment as divine self-revelation.
